title: Alegoria à Morte (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Death, part of a series of allegorical works by the French-Portuguese artist Quillard produced in Lisbon. Demonstrates the French-Portuguese artistic exchange in allegorical visual culture during the Baroque period.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria à Morte. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37491-alegoria-a-morte.

title: Alegoria ao Tempo (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Time, companion piece to the Alegoria à Morte. Part of Quillard's allegorical series produced in Lisbon. Time as a personified figure — part of the broader iconographic programme where abstract concepts (Justice, Time, Truth, Death) take human form.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria ao Tempo. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37507-alegoria-ao-tempo.

title: A Republica precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos
description: Electoral poster from the 1949 Portuguese presidential campaign featuring a female allegorical figure representing the Portuguese Republic. 'The Republic needs you: vote for Norton de Matos.' A classical female figure in robes symbolizes the Republic during a period of authoritarian governance — the allegory deployed as opposition to dictatorship.
citation_abnt: A REPUBLICA precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos. 1949. 1 cartaz. Comissão Distrital do Porto. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/.

title: 1 Escudo "Alvorada" — Primeira República Portuguesa
description: Figura feminina da República com barrete frígio, agitando tocha acesa, bandeira portuguesa no braço e sol nascente ao fundo. Inscrição: 5 DE OUTUBRO DE 1910. A "Alvorada" é a Marianne portuguesa: importação explícita da gramática visual republicana francesa adaptada à mitologia fundacional lusófona.
citation_abnt: 1 Escudo "Alvorada" — Primeira República Portuguesa

title: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa
description: Primeira série definitiva de selos após a proclamação da República, substituindo selos com retrato de D. Manuel II. Deusa romana Ceres de pé, segurando foice e feixe de trigo. A escolha de Ceres (abundância agrícola) sobre figura marcial reflete a narrativa republicana de soberania popular enraizada no trabalho.
citation_abnt: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa

title: La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme
description: Companion piece to FR-039. Liberty seated at center, flanked by standing Reason at left (with lion). Reason wields a radiant scepter/sun-disk emitting lightning bolts that strike Ignorance and Fanaticism (male/ambiguous figures recoiling at right). Liberty holds Reason's arm. Dark background, bas-relief composition. Inscription: 'La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme'.
citation_abnt: BOIZOT, Louis-Simon. La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme. 1793. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.

title: 25 Mark — Stadtsparkasse Bielefeld (Notgeld), Bielefelder Jungbronnen (Fountain of Youth), silk note
description: Weimar-era silk emergency currency (Notgeld) issued by Stadtsparkasse Bielefeld in 1921, celebrating the city's 700th anniversary. The obverse features a "Jungbrunnen" (fountain of youth) allegory: crippled figures enter a healing pool and emerge healed, with references to maidens keeping watch and medical attestations. The reverse offers a satirical commentary on local textile dye works polluting the Lutterbach river.
citation_abnt: STADTSPARKASSE BIELEFELD. 25 Mark (Notgeld). 1921. 1 cédula de seda (117 × 85 mm). Bielefeld, Alemanha. Catálogo Numista #210100. Disponível em: https://en.numista.com/210100.

title: Crispim do Amaral, Alegoria da República (pano de boca do Theatro da Paz, Belém, 1890), reproduzida em Lima Junior (2020)
description: Seated female allegory of the Brazilian Republic enthroned. Wears white classical dress with green mantle (national colors), laurel crown with red Phrygian cap, golden necklace. Right hand rests on a sword, left hand on the throne's armrest with lion-head finials. Palm frond at her feet. Background mosaic inscription 'ESTADOS UNIDOS DO BRASIL' with Roman numeral MDCCCLXXXIX (1889, date of Republic proclamation). Ornamental border with blue rosettes.
citation_abnt: LIMA JUNIOR, Carlos Rogério. Marianne à brasileira: imagens republicanas e os dilemas do Brasil nos finais do século XIX. 2020. Tese (Doutorado em História) — Faculdade de Filosofia, Letras e Ciências Humanas, Universidade de São Paulo, São Paulo, 2020. Reprodução: Alegoria da República (pano de boca do Theatro da Paz, Belém, 1890), de Crispim do Amaral.

title: Justitia enthroned, with sword and scales
description: Interior with Justitia enthroned, holding a sword and scales; female allegorical figures looking up to her and two putti holding shields. A formal composition of Justice as sovereign female judge.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA enthroned, with sword and scales. Século XVII. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1870-0625-185.

title: Providence and Justice (female personifications in niches)
description: Providence and Justice, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (ruler and scales, snake entwined around arm). Justice paired with Providence in architectural niches — the virtues as guardians of civic space.
citation_abnt: PROVIDENCE and Justice (personificações femininas em nichos). [s.d.]. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1862-0712-304.

title: Justitia and Prudentia (female personifications)
description: Justice and Prudence, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (sword and tablets of the law; mirror and snake). The cardinal-virtue pairing of Justice and Prudence as women.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA and Prudentia (personificações femininas). [s.d.]. 1 gravura. British Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_1862-0712-305.

title: Lady Justice (F.W. Pomeroy, Old Bailey, London)
description: The iconic gold statue of Lady Justice atop the Old Bailey, London's Central Criminal Court. Notably unblindfolded — holding sword and scales, with spiked crown. The courthouse brochures explain that 'her maidenly form is supposed to guarantee her impartiality.' A prime example of how the female body itself is argued to embody legal virtue.
citation_abnt: POMEROY, Frederick William. Lady Justice. 1907. 1 escultura em bronze dourado. Central Criminal Court (Old Bailey), London. Disponível em: http://www.speel.me.uk/sculptlondon/oldbaileyjustice.htm.

title: Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia)
description: Engraving by Étienne Delaune (c. 1560) depicting a female figure holding a sword and scales — the canonical attributes of Justice — identified as Jurisprudentia. Delaune was a French goldsmith and engraver active in mid-16th century France and Germany; this work, held at the Wellcome Collection, exemplifies Renaissance allegorical personification of law and jurisprudence.
citation_abnt: DELAUNE, Étienne. Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia). c. 1560. 1 gravura. Wellcome Collection, London. Disponível em: https://wellcomecollection.org/works/rkvhanzr.

title: Women of Britain Say 'Go!'
description: British WWI recruitment poster by E.J. Kealey (1915), published by the Parliamentary Recruiting Committee (Poster No. 75). Shows two women and a boy at an open window watching soldiers march away. The female figures embody a gendered allegory of domestic Britain urging men to enlist — deploying the moral authority of womanhood as surrogate for national female personification. One of the most iconic British WWI images, widely reproduced and analysed in the history of gender and war propaganda.
citation_abnt: KEALEY, Ernest James. Women of Britain say 'Go!'. 1915. 1 litografia colorida (cartaz). Imperial War Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.iwm.org.uk/collections/item/object/14592.

title: Take Up the Sword of Justice
description: Figura feminina de corpo inteiro personificando a Justiça ergue-se sobre o mar, estendendo espada embainhada. Abaixo, figuras afogando-se; ao fundo, o RMS Lusitania afundando. Parliamentary Recruiting Committee Poster No. 111.
citation_abnt: Take Up the Sword of Justice

title: America pois'd in the balance of justice
description: Revolutionary-era print showing two despondent women (possibly Britannia and America) in a rugged landscape, with ships and a burning city. The balance of justice as a geopolitical metaphor during the American Revolution.
citation_abnt: AMERICA pois'd in the balance of justice. 1776. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004673327/.

title: Justice and History (plaster model for US Capitol)
description: Photograph of plaster model for 'Justice and History' by Thomas Crawford, designed for the Senate bronze doors at the East Portico of the US Capitol. Justice and History as paired female figures guarding the entrance to the legislative chamber.
citation_abnt: CRAWFORD, Thomas. Justice and History (modelo para o Capitólio dos EUA). c. 1860. 1 fotografia (salt print). Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2009631377/.

title: Justice (blindfolded woman with sword and scales)
description: Official US government steel engraving of blindfolded Justice holding sword and scales. An institutional production of the legal allegory — the state manufacturing its own symbolic self-representation.
citation_abnt: JUSTICE (mulher vendada com espada e balança). [s.d.]. 1 gravura em aço. US Bureau of Printing & Engraving. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2007675578/.

title: Foire France-Américaine: Justice, Liberty, Demeter, Athena
description: WWI-era Franco-American poster showing four allegorical figures: Justice, Liberty (with American flag), Demeter, and Athena above Saint-Sulpice. The transatlantic circulation of female legal allegories during wartime.
citation_abnt: ROMBERG, Maurice. Foire France-Américaine: Justice, Liberty, Demeter, Athena. 1917. 1 litogravura colorida. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/99613542/.

title: Behold! a fabric now to freedom rear'd (Constitutional allegory)
description: Allegorical scene celebrating the US Constitution: Concord standing, Clio writing, Cupid holding the 'Constitution' before a pillar labeled 'Sacred to Liberty Justice and Peace' with thirteen columns. Female allegories deployed to sanctify the constitutional founding.
citation_abnt: TRENCHARD, James. Behold! a fabric now to freedom rear'd. 1788. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004676797/.

title: Die Wage der Macht / La balance de la puissance
description: Justice holding scales on which Britannia outweighs a Spaniard, Frenchman, America (as Native), and Dutchman. Justice as a geopolitical arbiter — weighing national power through the female allegorical figure. Bilingual (German/French) print.
citation_abnt: WILL, Johann Martin. Die Wage der Macht / La balance de la puissance. 1780. 1 gravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2004673370/.

title: Columbia presenting sword to Admiral Dewey
description: Columbia, the female personification of America, presenting a sword and crowning Admiral Dewey after the Spanish-American War. The martial dimension of the national female allegory — Columbia as warrior-queen bestowing military honors.
citation_abnt: COLUMBIA presenting sword to Admiral Dewey. 1899. 1 cromolitogravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018697020/.

title: Hedwig Reicher as Columbia in suffrage pageant
description: German actress Hedwig Reicher in costume as 'Columbia' at a suffrage pageant where Columbia summoned Justice, Charity, Liberty, Peace, and Hope to revive the crusade of women. A feminist reappropriation of national female allegory — Columbia mobilized for women's suffrage.
citation_abnt: HEDWIG Reicher as Columbia in suffrage pageant. 1913. 1 fotografia. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/97510759/.

title: The Goddess of Liberty (woman in star-spangled cape)
description: Photograph of a woman model in Liberty costume with stars, representing Liberty/Columbia during the Civil War era. The living body performing the allegory — a real woman embodying the national feminine symbol.
citation_abnt: THE GODDESS of Liberty (mulher com capa estrelada). 1861. 1 fotografia (carte de visite). Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018664118/.

title: Temple of Liberty
description: Woodcut broadside by Jared W. Bell (1834) depicting the Temple of Liberty as an allegorical female figure — the Goddess of Liberty — enthroned or standing within a classical temple. A key example of antebellum American female allegorical imagery deploying classical architecture and female personification to represent republican values and national identity.
citation_abnt: BELL, Jared W. Temple of liberty. 1834. 1 xilogravura. Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2008661765/.

title: Columbia Calls — Enlist Now for U.S. Army
description: Columbia sobre globo terrestre, posicionada na América do Norte, segurando bandeira americana e espada. 500.000 cópias impressas pelo U.S. War Department.
citation_abnt: Columbia Calls — Enlist Now for U.S. Army

title: Fight or Buy Bonds — Third Liberty Loan
description: Mulher de branco encarnando Liberty agita a bandeira americana enquanto soldados marcham atrás. A "Christy Girl" funde feminilidade idealizada com propósito marcial.
citation_abnt: Fight or Buy Bonds — Third Liberty Loan

title: Liberty Is Not Anarchy
description: Mãos desincorporadas de Columbia/Liberty agarrando anarquistas numa mão e espada "U.S." na outra, após o veredito de Haymarket. Columbia é reduzida a enormes mãos punitivas — sem rosto, sem corpo, apenas instrumentos de violência estatal.
citation_abnt: Liberty Is Not Anarchy

title: Looking Backward
description: Litografia colorida: americanos ricos — eles mesmos imigrantes ou filhos de imigrantes — bloqueiam um recém-chegado da Europa Oriental. Suas sombras na parede revelam origens humildes. Columbia está conspicuamente ausente da cena onde deveria aparecer como mãe acolhedora.
citation_abnt: Looking Backward
